title: The Glamping Mystery
subtitle_source: subs_resolved/0961.txt (396 dialogue lines, full transcript read)
notes: Recurring detective-cast nodes (Conan, Ran, Sonoko, Inspector Megure, Detective Takagi) omitted by convention; Sonoko is the one who actually delivers the solution on-screen this episode, but per the standing convention her deduction is represented only via the resulting edges, not a person node. case_type: murder. The old low-fidelity file (cases/ep961_the_glamping_mystery.json) got the culprit right (Mika Miura, s3/here p4) -- no identity correction needed. What it missed, corrected here: (1) it modeled a single generic location and a single 'murder' event/clue, collapsing away the episode's actual structure, which is a three-way body-relay -- Miura killed Keidai in her own tent, then each of the other two suspects independently found the body, tampered with it to frame someone else, and dumped it in a different tent, until it landed back in Miura's tent and finally in the open where the cast found it; that relay is now modeled as distinct `location` nodes and `frames`/`dumps_body_of`/`leaves_evidence` edges instead of being flattened. (2) the old file's single clue ('the specific allergen matches her breakup, a detail only she would know') is not quite what the transcript uses to convict her -- the actual clincher is behavioral exclusion (the two people who admitted knowing about the allergy were the least likely suspects; the real killer needed guilty knowledge without ever admitting it) plus a forensic cookie-bitterness comparison (fragments in Miura's tent tested non-bitter, matching Ran's plain chocolate cookies rather than the cacao-heavy batch needed to mask crab, disproving Miura's claim that no cookie evidence remained). Both are now separate `clue` nodes.
